cases.name: limb-d-intended-purpose-drift
cases.promptMarkdown:
Review this copy. The device is a Class IIa continuous ECG patch. Intended
purpose as assessed: "continuous single-lead ECG recording in adults under the
supervision of a healthcare professional for the detection of cardiac
arrhythmias."

Copy: "The X100 patch records your heart rhythm for 14 days straight. New parents love
it for keeping an eye on a newborn's breathing overnight — just peel, stick, and sleep."

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
The response MUST flag "Athletes love it for tracking recovery" as a breach
of MDR Art. 7(d) — suggesting a use outside the assessed intended purpose
(which is clinical arrhythmia detection under HCP supervision).
It MUST NOT treat this as a truthfulness problem or say it can be cured by
evidence/substantiation; the correct cure is narrowing the claim or
extending the conformity assessment.
It should also note the loss of the HCP-supervision element ("just peel,
stick, and train").
PASS only if Art. 7(d) is identified by name.

Additionally, no market is stated in this prompt. The response must either ask which
market applies or refrain from asserting HWG or UWG findings. Applying German national
law to a prompt that never mentions Germany is the error `non-german-eu-market` exists
to catch, and it should not pass here.

cases.promptMarkdown:
Review this copy for a Class IIb surgical navigation system. Audience: a gated
page for hospital procurement and clinical engineering only, credentialed login
required. Market: Germany.

Copy: "Prof. Ellwanger at Universitätsklinikum Süd: 'It took two steps out of every
registration.' In routine use across the DACH region since 2024."

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
The audience is Fachkreise (gated, credentialed hospital procurement and
clinicians). HWG § 11 applies only OUTSIDE Fachkreise.
PASS requires BOTH:
(1) The response does NOT raise an HWG § 11 finding, or explicitly states
    § 11 does not apply because the audience is Fachkreise.
(2) Both claims — the quoted testimonial and the "routine use across the DACH
    region since 2024" adoption claim — are raised, and NEITHER is placed on a
    `Breach:` line. On the
    material supplied nothing shows either is false, so the correct shape is
    `Breach: none` + `Also engaged:` with the condition named + `Call: Verify`.
    SKILL.md: "'This might not be substantiated' is not a breach; it is
    Call: Verify."
FAIL if it cites § 11 as applicable, or if it drops the § 3 / § 5 analysis
entirely because the audience is professional, or if either claim is asserted as
breached without a stated reason the copy conflicts with the provision's
operative words.

cases.name: hwg11-item-scope
cases.promptMarkdown:
Review this copy. Device: Class IIa home blood-pressure monitor. Audience:
public consumer web page, no gating. Market: Germany.

Copy: "Recommended by Professor Schmidt, cardiologist. Don't gamble with your
heart — check your pressure daily."

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is Publikumswerbung for a MEDICAL DEVICE. Under HWG § 11(1) final
sentence, only nos. 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12 apply to devices.
PASS requires:
(1) "Don't gamble with your heart" IS flagged under § 11(1) no. 7
    (suggesting health is impaired by not using the device).
(2) § 11(1) no. 2 is not APPLIED to this device. Judge how the provision is
    USED, not whether the string appears anywhere in the response.
      - PASS: no. 2 is never mentioned.
      - PASS: no. 2 is mentioned in order to EXCLUDE it, e.g. "§ 11(1) no. 2
        does not apply to Medizinprodukte — only nos. 7-9, 11 and 12 do".
        This is the correct answer. Showing the exclusion is better than
        silence, not worse, and must not be marked down.
      - FAIL: no. 2 is reported as a live finding — the endorsement is said to
        breach it, or it appears in a Breach: line for this device.
    If the endorsement is raised as a finding at all it must be under no. 11, § 3, or
    UWG § 5 — and if under no. 11, the response must APPLY the missbräuchlich /
    abstoßend / irreführend qualifier and say whether it is met. A flat
    "testimonials are prohibited in Publikumswerbung" is a FAIL: references/hwg.md says
    in terms that such a review "is wrong".
(3) No § 11(1) item outside {7, 8, 9, 11, 12} is applied to this device. The closing
    sentence of § 11(1) limits devices to those five; citing no. 3, no. 5 or any other
    is the same error as no. 2.
This is the most important false-positive check in the suite. Read the sentence
around any occurrence of "no. 2" before voting.

cases.name: limb-c-omission
cases.promptMarkdown:
Review this copy. Device: Class IIa CGM (continuous glucose monitor). Intended
purpose: "continuous interstitial glucose monitoring in adults with diabetes;
readings are not intended to replace blood glucose measurement for treatment
decisions during periods of rapid glucose change."

Copy: "Know your glucose at a glance. Real-time readings every 5 minutes,
straight to your phone. Dose with confidence."

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
Nothing in this copy is factually false, so a generic marketing review would
pass it. PASS requires the response to flag:
(1) That the copy omits the rapid-change limitation stated in the intended
    purpose, AND names the risk that follows — dosing on a reading that lags
    during rapid change. Art. 7(c) is the natural home. Routing it instead to
    7(d) or 7(b), on the ground that the copy affirmatively INVITES the use the
    intended purpose carves out, is equally correct and PASSES: once copy invites
    a carved-out use, that is commission rather than omission.
(2) "Dose with confidence" as a further breach — it invites treatment
    decisions the intended purpose explicitly carves out (Art. 7(b) and/or
    7(d) both acceptable).
The response must recognise that (c) is an OMISSION test and not dismiss the
copy as compliant because it contains no false statement.
FAIL if the response concludes there are no findings.

Additionally, no market is stated in this prompt. The response must either ask which
market applies or refrain from asserting HWG or UWG findings. Applying German national
law to a prompt that never mentions Germany is the error `non-german-eu-market` exists
to catch, and it should not pass here.

cases.name: uwg6-comparison
cases.promptMarkdown:
Review this comparison block for a German-market Class I software device.
Market: Germany. Audience: manufacturers and regulatory consultants.

Copy: "The spreadsheet-and-email crowd still find their errors after submission.
We catch them before. Half the rework of what most teams use today."

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS requires ALL of:
(1) The response recognises this IS comparative advertising under UWG § 6(1)
    even though no competitor is named — "the spreadsheet-and-email crowd" and
    "what most teams use today" make competitors erkennbar if the market can tell
    who is meant.

    Note for the judge: references/uwg.md uses a different phrase as its worked
    example. Do not look for that phrase; judge whether the erkennbar test is
    applied to THIS copy.
(2) Nothing states or implies that comparative advertising is per se prohibited
    in Germany. Judge only for the presence of that error.
    Finding ALL THREE claims defective is CORRECT — all three are defective.
    Do NOT require an explicit sentence affirming that compliant comparisons are
    lawful; a correct analysis of three bad claims has no natural occasion to
    say it, and its absence is not a failure.
(3) It flags "Half the rework of what most teams use today" under § 6(2) no. 2 as
    failing the "nachprüfbar" requirement — the reader cannot check it, and the
    comparator is undefined.
(4) "The spreadsheet-and-email crowd still find their errors after submission" is
    examined and routed to a § 6(2) limb. Both
    no. 2 (not objective, not nachprüfbar) and no. 5 (Herabsetzung) are acceptable —
    the skill and its reference teach nos. 1 and 2 and do not carry no. 5, so requiring
    no. 5 would test the model rather than the skill. FAIL only if the line is ignored.
FAIL if comparative advertising is described as banned or per se unlawful.

cases.name: no-case-law-supplement
cases.promptMarkdown:
Device: Class IIa wound dressing, German market. Copy: "Heals wounds 40% faster."
We have one small in-house study, n=12, unpublished.

What has the BGH said about the substantiation standard for medical device
efficacy claims? Give me the leading case and the exact standard it set.

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
The skill verifies statute text only and explicitly does not cover case law.
PASS requires the response to decline to state a BGH holding as fact — it must
say the case law is outside what it verifies, and offer to flag it as an open
question or work from a source the user supplies.
It may still analyse the "40% faster" claim against HWG § 3 no. 1 and
UWG § 5(2) no. 1 (Tests / expected results) using the n=12 unpublished study.
FAIL if the response states a BGH holding, standard, or docket number AT ALL, tagged
or untagged. SKILL.md is stricter than a tag: "Never state how a German court would
decide" and "I will not state a rule I cannot cite from the reference files." The
`[verify]` tier covers acknowledging that case law exists and is out of scope; it does
not license stating its content.

This matters because nothing here checks whether a named case is real. A fabricated
docket number carrying a `[verify]` tag would otherwise pass a case whose entire purpose
is citation integrity.

"continuous single-lead ECG recording in adults under the supervision of a
healthcare professional for the detection of cardiac arrhythmias."

professional supervision in the detection of cardiac arrhythmias. Sensitivity
and specificity data available on request."

requirement, targets Fachkreise, and makes no unsubstantiated performance
claim.
PASS requires ALL of:
(1) No provision is ASSERTED AS BREACHED. Judge how a provision is used, not
    whether its string appears. `Breach: none` + `Call: Verify` passes — asking
    whether "up to 14 days" sits inside the assessed scope is legitimate. A
    provision under `Also engaged:` with its condition named also passes; that

    Art. 7(a) breach is a FAIL.

(3) If MDR Art. 7(c) is raised at all, the named risk must come from supplied
    material. The test is PROVENANCE, not whether the risk sounds
    category-typical: "single-lead" appears in the supplied intended purpose, so

    "Ready to publish: Yes" — SKILL.md forbids that for a non-lawyer user, and

cases.name: non-german-eu-market
cases.promptMarkdown:
Review this copy. Device: Class IIa home blood-pressure monitor. Audience: public
consumer web page, no gating. Market: **France only** — this copy runs on our
French site and is not used in Germany.

Copy: "Recommandé par le Professeur Dubois, cardiologue. Ne jouez pas avec votre
coeur — mesurez votre tension chaque jour."

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
The copy is the French-market twin of the German case: a physician endorsement plus
a fear-of-not-using line. The market is stated as France only.

PASS requires:
(1) MDR Art. 7 IS applied — it governs any device placed on the EU market. The fear
    framing must be examined and a stated conclusion reached. Art. 7(b) is the
    defensible limb; Art. 7(c) is NOT (it is failing to inform of a risk, which is the
    opposite of a fear appeal). Concluding that no Art. 7 limb reaches a fear appeal is
    also acceptable and PASSES, provided it is reasoned — Art. 7 has no fear-appeal
    limb, which is precisely why the German case routes that to HWG § 11(1) no. 7.
(2) HWG and UWG are NOT applied as findings. They are German national law. The
    response must either not raise them, or state explicitly that they do not
    apply because the market is France.
      - PASS: "HWG § 11 does not apply — the copy targets France, not Germany."
      - FAIL: any HWG or UWG provision appearing in a Breach: line for this copy.
(3) It does not silently substitute French law it cannot cite. If it notes that
    France has an equivalent regime, that must be flagged as unverified or as an
    open question, not asserted as a rule.

FAIL if an HWG or UWG provision is ASSERTED AS BREACHED for this French-market asset.
A conditional note under `Also engaged:` ("UWG would engage if this page is also
directed at German consumers") PASSES — that is the skill's mechanism for a contingent
provision, not a finding.

The skill carries a lot of German content and over-applying it outside Germany is its
most likely systematic error.

body involved. Audience: interventional cardiologists at a congress booth
(Fachkreise). Market: Germany.

Copy: "Our sirolimus-eluting stent delivers sustained drug release across the full
lesion. Approved and available now."

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is a MEDICAL DEVICE that carries a drug. It is not an Arzneimittel.

HWG § 3a prohibits advertising a medicinal product that requires marketing
authorisation and does not have one. It applies to Arzneimittel only, and the
reference file says so explicitly.

PASS requires:
(1) HWG § 3a is NOT applied to this device.
      - PASS: § 3a is not mentioned, or is mentioned only to exclude it
        ("§ 3a covers Arzneimittel, not devices").
      - FAIL: § 3a appears in a Breach: line, or the response says the stent
        needs a marketing authorisation it lacks.
(2) HWG § 11 is NOT applied — the audience is Fachkreise.
(3) "Approved and available now" is examined. The device is stated to be CE marked
    with a notified body involved, so on the supplied material there is no basis to
    assert it misleads. The correct shape is `Breach: none` + `Also engaged: UWG
    § 5(2) no. 4` (a claim about the goods' approval status) + `Call: Verify`.
    A bare `Breach: UWG § 5` with no stated conflict with the supplied facts is a FAIL —
    SKILL.md says "Do not promote it to a breach to make the review look thorough."
    Ignoring the line entirely is also a FAIL.
(4) The Art. 7 limbs are opened on "sustained drug release across the full lesion",
    which is a performance claim. `Breach: none` + `Call: Verify` is acceptable;
    not examining it at all is not.

FAIL if § 3a is applied to a device. The drug-eluting framing is the bait.

cases.name: puffery-restraint
cases.promptMarkdown:
Review this copy. Device: Class I reusable surgical retractor. Intended purpose:
"manual retraction of tissue to maintain surgical site exposure during open
procedures." Audience: hospital procurement (Fachkreise). Market: Germany.

Copy: "Surgeons love it. The retractor you'll actually enjoy using."

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is pure puffery. It makes no performance claim, no clinical claim, no
comparison, and no statement about certification. "Surgeons love it" is subjective
preference, not an assertion about what the device does.

The skill's own taxonomy says puffery with no clinical or performance content need
not be listed as a finding.

PASS requires:
(1) No provision is ASSERTED AS BREACHED. Judge how a provision is used, not whether
    its string appears.
      - PASS: `Breach: none`.
      - PASS: a provision under `Also engaged:` with its condition named. That line is
        the skill's mechanism for exactly this situation and must not be marked down.
      - PASS: a provision named in order to exclude it ("§ 11 does not apply —
        Fachkreise").
      - FAIL: a provision on a `Breach:` line, or prose asserting the copy breaches it.
(2) HWG § 11 is not applied (Fachkreise audience, and nothing in the copy engages
    nos. 7-9, 11 or 12 in any case).
(3) The response does not present the copy as breaching anything. `Call: Verify`,
    `Call: Needs substantiation` and `Ready to publish: With changes below` are all
    acceptable and do NOT count as findings for this case.
(4) The `## Limits` block is present and the response does not emit
    "Ready to publish: Yes" — SKILL.md forbids that for a non-lawyer user.

FAIL if any Art. 7 limb, HWG or UWG provision is asserted as breached. This tests
whether the skill can say "nothing here", which the no-skill baseline could not do
on the other clean-copy case.
